events.text:
Here is the comparison for Erfurt.

## How Britannica described Erfurt

Britannica (1771–1797), entry **ERFURT** `[B:2473:9]`, is a single short entry (147 chars):

> "ERFURT, a large and beautiful city of Upper Saxony in Germany, capital of Thailand, and subject to the elckor of Menus; E. long.117 é', N.lax. 910."

That text is raw OCR with errors. Reading the page scan, the passage actually says **capital of Thuringia** (not Thailand), **Elector of Menus** (= Elector of Mainz), and coordinates of roughly **E. long. 11°, N. lat. 50°** (the OCR mangled "11° 17'" as "117 é'" and "50° ..." as "910"). So Britannica describes Erfurt as a large and beautiful city of Upper Saxony in Germany, capital of Thuringia, subject to the Elector of Mainz, at about 11°E, 50°N `[B:2473:9]`.

## Match to Wikipedia

`get_pair` matched the entry to the Wikipedia article Erfurt `[W:9481:1352872890]` (status: matched; rerank logit −5.81, margin 1.51; not flagged low-confidence, though the entry is tiny and OCR-garbled, so treat with caution).

## Which Britannica facts are superseded

The comparison checked 5 claims: **4 superseded, 1 dropped, 0 enduring, 0 renamed** (superseded share 0.8) `[B:2473:9][W:9481:1352872890]`.

| Britannica claim | Tag | What Wikipedia says instead |
|---|---|---|
| Erfurt is a large and beautiful city of Upper Saxony, Germany | superseded | "capital and largest city of the Central German state of Thuringia" `[W:9481:1352872890]` |
| Erfurt is the capital of Thailand | superseded | capital of Thuringia (this is an OCR error for "Thuringia" in the scan) `[B:2473:9][W:9481:1352872890]` |
| Erfurt is at East longitude 117 degrees | superseded | Erfurt lies in the River Gera valley, southern Thuringian Basin; 100 km SW of Leipzig, 250 km NE of Frankfurt `[W:9481:1352872890]` |
| Erfurt is at North latitude 910 | superseded | same Wikipedia location passage `[W:9481:1352872890]` |
| Erfurt is subject to the Elector of Mainz | dropped | Wikipedia treats the Electorate of Mainz as history (part of the HRE; part of Prussia from 1802; GDR 1949–1990), not a current fact `[W:9481:1352872890]` |

Lexical drift pairs the system found: "Upper Saxony" → "Thuringia"; "elckor of Menus" → "Electorate of Mainz" `[B:2473:9][W:9481:1352872890]`.

Inference: once the OCR errors are corrected against the scan, the real knowledge drift is not that Erfurt moved or changed its capital status, but the regional label (Upper Saxony → Thuringia) and the political succession (Electorate of Mainz → Kingdom of Prussia 1802 → Thuringia state capital today). Wikipedia adds extensive coverage Britannica lacks: modern population (~216,000), economy, university history (1379/1816/1994), landmarks (Krämerbrücke, cathedral, Petersberg Citadel, UNESCO Jewish-Medieval Heritage), and 20th-century history `[W:9481:1352872890]`.

**Citations:** Britannica `[B:2473:9]`; Wikipedia `[W:9481:1352872890]` (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erfurt, revision 1352872890).
